clauses.reason: Terminated by own terms: 'until May 1, 1936' (stated date inclusive, 1936-05-01; exclusive reading one day earlier). Actor EO:7217 itself. No later order names this order or the person in any held text; the chain ends here.

research_rationale:
EO:7217 (1935-10-30) is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 exempting Carleton W. Sturtevant from compulsory retirement for age and continuing the person in the service 'until May 1, 1936'. The order ends by its own terms on 1936-05-01 (stated date, inclusive; exclusive alternative one day earlier, per the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on 'until' dates). Later orders in the same person's exemption chain, read in the packet: none held; each is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote (owner ruling, 2026-10-21), and none revokes, amends or shortens this order. Last held order in the Sturtevant chain (EO 6577 → 6773 → 7217). jobs/namier finds no later held text naming Carleton W. Sturtevant; the OFR catalog starts after this order's end. Whether he separated on or before May 1, 1936 is not in any held source and is not asserted. The dossier's machine term leads were read against the text; the operative until-date in the command sentence is the end. @rationale:retirement:statute @rationale:retirement:search @rationale:retirement:inventory

savings.reason: Service performed and compensation earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects of the person's continued employment; the order creates no continuing duty, office or rule after its stated term. A later 'further' exemption of the same person is a new grant under the statute, not a savings clause of this order, and the person's employment after the stated date rests on that later order, not on this one.
